sentences.asr: should all university students be required to learn academic writing.
A recent proposal says yes, and I strongly support it. For academic writing is a basic skill that every student needs, regardless of major.
First of all, academic writing is essential for university study itself.
Students must be able to present ideas clearly, organize arguments logically and cite sources properly, whether they are writing a lab report, a course paper or a graduation thesis.
Without systematic training, many students simply copy information from the internet or make claims without evidence.
Moreover, learning to write academically sharpens critical thinking.
To produce a convincing paper, students have to evaluate evidence, compare different views and draw sound conclusions. Skills that are valuable in any career.
To be effective. However an academic writing course should be designed to meet the needs of different majors.
Engineering students, for instance, may focus on technical reports and data presentation, while literature students may practice writing critical essays.
With such flexibility, the requirement will truly benefit every student.
Is technology making people lazy?
It is often claimed that computers leave people easily distracted, mentally lazy, and less efficient at work.
In my view, technology itself does not make people lazy. What matters is how they use it.
It is true that technology can encourage laziness.
With search engines at hand, some people no longer bother to remember facts or think problems through.
Others rely on navigation apps for every trip and rarely try to find their own way.
Constant messages and pop-up advertisements also interrupt their work, making it hard to concentrate and lowering their efficiency.
On the other hand, technology can make people more productive when it is used wisely.
It frees people from repetitive tasks such as calculating figures and copying documents, giving them more time for creative work.
Online courses and digital libraries also allow them to learn new skills and explore new fields whenever and wherever they like.
The K, therefore is self-discipline.
If people treat technology as a tool rather than a crutch, it will make them smarter, not lazier.
